project.name: Brightsmile Dental online booking
project.description: Patients book dental appointments online instead of phoning the front desk.
project.business_problem: Patients can only book by phoning the front desk during opening hours.
business_objectives: Let patients book appointments outside opening hours without phoning

requirements.title: Book an appointment online
requirements.description: A patient books an appointment by choosing a dentist, a treatment type and a free time slot from the calendar.
requirements.evidence: The patient picks a dentist, a treatment type and a free time slot from the calendar.
acceptance_criteria: Given a patient on the booking page, when they select a dentist, treatment and free slot and confirm, then the appointment is saved and the slot is no longer shown as free.
requirements.priority_reason: This is the goal of US-001; without it the story delivers nothing.

requirements.title: Send booking confirmation email
requirements.description: After a booking is saved, the patient receives a confirmation email stating the appointment date, time and dentist.
requirements.evidence: After booking, the patient receives a confirmation email with the date, time and dentist.
acceptance_criteria: Given a patient has confirmed a booking When the appointment is saved Then the patient receives an email showing the appointment date, time and dentist
requirements.priority_reason: The client says patients "should" get a confirmation. Booking still works without it, but it is small and builds on FR-001, so it is proposed for MVP.

requirements.title: Booking window of 24 hours to 60 days
requirements.description: An appointment can be booked only if its start time is at least 24 hours and at most 60 days after the moment of booking.
requirements.evidence: Appointments can only be booked between 24 hours and 60 days in advance.
acceptance_criteria: Given a slot less than 24 hours away, when the patient views the calendar, then the slot cannot be selected.
requirements.priority_reason: The client says bookings "can only" be made 24 hours to 60 days ahead, and FR-001 (MUST) is governed by it.

requirements.title: A booked slot is no longer free
requirements.description: Once an appointment is saved for a slot, that slot is no longer offered as free to any patient.
requirements.evidence: the slot is no longer shown as free
acceptance_criteria: Given a slot has just been booked, when another patient views the calendar, then that slot is not shown as free.
requirements.priority_reason: FR-001 (MUST) is governed by it; without it a slot could be booked twice.

requirements.title: Booking page load time
requirements.description: The booking page loads fast on desktop and mobile. The target load time is not stated.

nfr_metric.metric: booking page load time on mobile
nfr_metric.measurement: UNKNOWN — to be agreed with the client (see Q-001)

requirements.evidence: The booking page should load fast, even on mobile.
requirements.priority_reason: The story says the page "should load fast". It is proposed for MVP because it measures FR-001, but it cannot be approved until Q-001 gives a target.

requirements.title: ClinicDesk remains the master calendar
requirements.description: The existing practice-management system, ClinicDesk, stays the master calendar. The booking feature must not replace it.
requirements.evidence: We must keep using our existing practice-management system (ClinicDesk) as the master calendar.
requirements.priority_reason: The client says "We must keep using" ClinicDesk; every booking design depends on it.

requirements.title: Read availability from and write bookings to ClinicDesk
requirements.description: Online booking reads free slots from ClinicDesk and writes each confirmed appointment back to ClinicDesk.
requirements.rationale: CON-001 makes ClinicDesk the master calendar, so the free slots shown in FR-001 must come from ClinicDesk, and new bookings must land there or the calendars diverge.
requirements.scope_reason: Follows from in-scope items (CON-001); needed for them to work.
requirements.priority_reason: FR-001 (MUST) depends on it, and a MUST item's dependencies are MUST.

ambiguities.what: "a treatment type" does not say which treatments are bookable online.
ambiguities.why_it_matters: It decides which treatments the booking page lists and which ClinicDesk appointment types are exposed.
interpretations: Only cleanings and check-ups (the story's "I want" names these)
ambiguities.question: Q-002
ambiguities.impact_if_unresolved: The booking page may offer treatments the practice wants handled by phone.

ambiguities.what: "a free time slot" does not say how long a slot is.
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Slot length decides how the calendar is cut up and whether a longer treatment fits.
interpretations: One fixed slot length for all treatments
Slot length depends on the treatment type
ambiguities.question: Q-003
ambiguities.impact_if_unresolved: Appointments may overlap or leave gaps in the dentist's day.

ambiguities.why_it_matters: Without a number the requirement cannot be tested or designed for.
interpretations: Faster than the current phone wait, with no fixed number
ambiguities.question: Q-001
ambiguities.impact_if_unresolved: NFR-001 stays untestable and may be judged failed at acceptance.

gaps.description: The story does not say how a patient is identified when booking.
gaps.why_relevant_to_domain: healthcare: a booking is tied to a patient record, and booking under someone else's name exposes health data.
gaps.question: Q-004

gaps.description: No health-data or privacy regulation is named. SECURITY, AUDIT_LOGGING and DATA_RETENTION obligations follow from the answer, so they are covered by this gap.
gaps.why_relevant_to_domain: healthcare: appointment data and treatment type are health data in most jurisdictions.
gaps.question: Q-005

gaps.description: Reminders are listed as undecided in the story's Open points.
gaps.why_relevant_to_domain: appointment-scheduling: reminders are the usual way to cut no-shows.
gaps.question: Q-006

gaps.description: Online cancellation and rescheduling are listed as undecided in the story's Open points.
gaps.why_relevant_to_domain: appointment-scheduling: patients expect to change a booking the same way they made it.
gaps.question: Q-007

gaps.description: No behaviour is given for ClinicDesk being unreachable, two simultaneous bookings of one slot, or a failed confirmation email.
gaps.why_relevant_to_domain: appointment-scheduling with an external master calendar: both failures are common.
gaps.question: Q-008

gaps.description: No accessibility standard is given for a public booking page.
gaps.why_relevant_to_domain: healthcare: patients include older people and people with impairments, who must be able to book.
gaps.question: Q-009

questions.text: What load time should the booking page meet on mobile, and on what kind of connection should it be measured?
questions.suggested_default_option: Option: page interactive within 3 s on a mid-range phone over 4G (p75 of real visits)
options: Other target set by the client

questions.text: Which treatment types can patients book online: only cleanings and check-ups, or every treatment the practice offers?
questions.suggested_default_option: Option: only cleanings and check-ups, as named in the story; other treatments stay phone-only

questions.text: How long is a bookable slot: one fixed length, or does it depend on the treatment?
questions.suggested_default_option: Option: length depends on treatment type and is taken from ClinicDesk

questions.text: How does a patient identify themselves when booking: an online account, or details checked against ClinicDesk (e.g. name, date of birth, phone)?
questions.suggested_default_option: Option: no account; match name, date of birth and phone against the ClinicDesk patient record

questions.text: In which country does the practice operate, and which health-data regulations apply to booking data?
questions.suggested_default_option: Option: the client names the jurisdiction; the team then lists the obligations for review

questions.text: Should patients receive appointment reminders, and if so by which channel and how far in advance?
questions.suggested_default_option: Option: no reminders in the first release; revisit after launch

questions.text: Can patients cancel or reschedule online, and up to how long before the appointment?
questions.suggested_default_option: Option: no online cancellation in the first release; patients phone the front desk
options: Cancel online up to 24 hours before

questions.text: What happens when ClinicDesk is unreachable, when two people book the same slot at the same moment, or when the confirmation email cannot be sent?
questions.suggested_default_option: Option: show the patient a "try again or phone us" message; ClinicDesk decides which booking wins

questions.text: Which accessibility standard should the booking page meet?

risks.title: ClinicDesk may not support reading slots or writing bookings
risks.description: IR-001 assumes ClinicDesk exposes availability and accepts new appointments from outside. If it does not, online booking cannot work as specified.
risks.mitigation: Confirm ClinicDesk API access and terms with the vendor before design starts; plan a short technical spike.
risks.rationale: CON-001 fixes ClinicDesk as master calendar, so the whole feature depends on its integration options, which the stories do not describe.

risks.title: Double booking between online and front desk
risks.description: A slot can be booked online and at the front desk at the same moment, breaking BR-002.
risks.mitigation: Make ClinicDesk the single place a booking is committed and re-check availability at confirmation (see Q-008).
risks.rationale: Two booking channels write to one calendar.

risks.title: Health-data obligations unknown
risks.description: Booking stores patient identity with a treatment type. The applicable regulation is not known (Q-005).
risks.mitigation: Get the jurisdiction from the client early and review obligations before architecture work.
risks.rationale: healthcare domain with no regulation named.

risks.title: Page-speed requirement cannot be tested yet
risks.description: NFR-001 has no target, so it cannot pass or fail acceptance.
risks.mitigation: Agree a target through Q-001 before the requirement is approved.

innovations.title: Automatic reminders
innovations.description: Send reminders before due dates or appointments on the user's chosen channel.
innovations.problem_solved: Patients forget appointments booked weeks in advance.
innovations.business_value: Fewer no-shows and empty chair time.
innovations.user_value: A timely nudge before the visit.
innovations.relevance_reason: Reminders are the client's own open point (Q-006); dental check-ups are booked weeks ahead.

innovations.title: Personal calendar sync
innovations.description: Add bookings to Google, Apple or Outlook calendars with updates.
innovations.problem_solved: The appointment is not in the patient's own calendar.
innovations.business_value: Fewer missed visits at almost no cost.
innovations.user_value: One tap adds the visit to their calendar.
innovations.relevance_reason: Bookings are made far ahead; patients keep their own calendars.

innovations.title: Core Web Vitals budget
innovations.description: Set and enforce load-time budgets in the build pipeline.
innovations.problem_solved: "Load fast" has no shared measure.
innovations.user_value: A quick page on phones.
innovations.relevance_reason: Gives NFR-001 a measurable yardstick once the client sets a target.

innovations.title: Skeleton loading screens
innovations.description: Show the page layout immediately while data loads to cut perceived wait.
innovations.problem_solved: Blank screen while slots load.
innovations.business_value: Lower drop-off on the booking page.
innovations.user_value: The page feels instant.
innovations.relevance_reason: Availability comes from ClinicDesk and may take a moment to load.

innovations.title: Passwordless magic links
innovations.description: Sign in or confirm identity by a one-time link sent by email or SMS.
innovations.problem_solved: Patients do not want another password for a twice-yearly visit.
innovations.business_value: Identity check without account support load.
innovations.user_value: Confirm a booking from their inbox.
innovations.relevance_reason: One of the answers to Q-004 (how patients identify) without passwords.

innovations.title: One-tap reschedule links
innovations.description: Include a secure link in messages that lets people move their booking.
innovations.problem_solved: Changing an appointment needs a phone call.
innovations.user_value: Move a visit without calling.
innovations.relevance_reason: Relevant only if the client allows online changes (Q-007).

innovations.title: Funnel analytics
innovations.description: Track where users drop out of key flows such as sign-up or booking.
innovations.problem_solved: No evidence of where patients give up.
innovations.business_value: Proves the business case of online booking.
innovations.user_value: Indirect: a smoother flow over time.
innovations.relevance_reason: Shows whether online booking actually replaces phone calls, the client's stated goal.

innovations.title: Post-visit reviews
innovations.description: Ask for a rating after a visit or order and route low scores to staff.
innovations.problem_solved: Happy patients rarely leave reviews unprompted.
innovations.user_value: An easy way to give feedback.
innovations.relevance_reason: Local practices win new patients through reviews.

innovations.title: Bot and abuse protection
innovations.description: Stop automated sign-ups, scraping and fake bookings without CAPTCHAs for most users.
innovations.problem_solved: Bots or pranksters can fill the calendar.
innovations.user_value: Real slots stay available.
innovations.relevance_reason: A public booking page without login (Q-004 open) invites fake bookings.

innovations.title: QR code check-in
innovations.description: Check in on arrival by scanning a QR code.
innovations.problem_solved: Patients queue at reception to say they have arrived.
innovations.user_value: Check in without queuing.
innovations.relevance_reason: The front desk is swamped; self check-in removes one task.

innovations.title: Preferred provider memory
innovations.description: Remember the person's preferred professional or location and default to it.
innovations.problem_solved: Patients pick their dentist again every time.
innovations.user_value: Their dentist is pre-selected.
innovations.relevance_reason: Patients usually return to the same dentist; needs a way to recognise them (Q-004).

innovations.title: Visual availability calendar
innovations.description: Show free slots across days at a glance with the soonest option highlighted.
innovations.problem_solved: Hunting day by day for a free slot.
innovations.user_value: See the soonest slot at a glance.
innovations.relevance_reason: FR-001 is a calendar pick; showing several days at once helps patients find a slot fast.

innovations.title: Cached availability with live confirm
innovations.description: Show availability from a fast cache and confirm against the master system at checkout.
innovations.problem_solved: Every page view queries ClinicDesk live.
innovations.user_value: Slots appear quickly.
innovations.relevance_reason: ClinicDesk may be slow or rate-limited (RISK-001); a cache with live confirmation protects NFR-001.

innovations.title: Graceful degradation
innovations.description: Keep core flows usable when a dependency fails, with clear fallback messages.
innovations.problem_solved: A ClinicDesk outage breaks booking with no explanation.
innovations.business_value: Bookings fall back to phone gracefully, not lost.
innovations.user_value: A clear message instead of an error page.
innovations.relevance_reason: Directly addresses the ERROR_HANDLING gap (Q-008).

innovations.title: Waitlist with automatic offers
innovations.description: When a slot or item frees up, offer it to the next person on the waitlist.
innovations.problem_solved: Cancelled slots stay empty.
innovations.user_value: Get an earlier slot when one frees up.
innovations.relevance_reason: Popular slots fill quickly; cancellations otherwise go unused.

innovations.title: Recall and re-engagement campaigns
innovations.description: Invite customers back when a periodic visit or renewal is due.
innovations.problem_solved: Patients forget their next check-up is due.
innovations.user_value: A reminder when a check-up is due, with a booking link.
innovations.relevance_reason: Dental check-ups recur every 6–12 months; visit history sits in ClinicDesk.

innovations.title: Pre-visit digital intake
innovations.description: Collect forms and consents before the visit instead of on paper at reception.
innovations.problem_solved: Paper forms at reception slow the front desk.
innovations.user_value: Fill forms at home.
innovations.relevance_reason: Health questionnaires are filled at reception today; they could be done after booking.

innovations.title: Embeddable booking widget
innovations.description: Let partners or the client's own site embed booking.
innovations.problem_solved: Patients must find a separate booking site.
innovations.business_value: More bookings from the existing website.
innovations.user_value: Book from the practice website directly.
innovations.relevance_reason: The practice likely has a website where booking should live.

innovations.title: WhatsApp and SMS channels
innovations.description: Message customers on the channels they already use.
innovations.problem_solved: Emails go unread.
innovations.user_value: Messages on the channel they use.
innovations.relevance_reason: Confirmations and reminders may reach patients better by SMS or WhatsApp than email.

innovations.title: Accessible design system
innovations.description: Shared components that meet WCAG 2.2 AA by default.
innovations.problem_solved: Accessibility fixed screen by screen, late.
innovations.user_value: Usable with screen readers and large text.
innovations.relevance_reason: Supports whichever accessibility standard Q-009 settles on.

innovations.title: Consent management
innovations.description: Record and honour each person's consents with history.
innovations.problem_solved: Consent is not recorded anywhere.
innovations.user_value: Control over how they are contacted.
risks: Consents out of sync across systems
innovations.relevance_reason: Health data and patient messaging both need recorded consent once the regime is known (Q-005).

innovations.title: Tamper-evident audit trail
innovations.description: Record who viewed or changed what, in a log that cannot be edited.
innovations.problem_solved: No record of who saw or changed a booking.
innovations.user_value: Trust that their data is watched.
innovations.relevance_reason: Healthcare regimes usually require knowing who accessed booking data (Q-005).

innovations.title: Capacity utilisation report
innovations.description: Show how full calendars, rooms or vehicles are, by hour and resource.
innovations.problem_solved: No view of empty chair time.
innovations.user_value: Indirect: more convenient hours offered.
innovations.relevance_reason: The practice can see which dentists and hours are under-booked.

innovations.title: Recurring bookings and orders
innovations.description: Set up repeating appointments, orders or tasks once.
innovations.problem_solved: Patients rebook the same check-up every time.
innovations.user_value: Book the series once.
innovations.relevance_reason: Regular check-ups could be booked as a series, limited by the 60-day window (BR-001).

innovations.title: Book from search and maps
innovations.description: Let people book directly from search-engine and map listings.
innovations.problem_solved: New patients leave search to find a booking page.
innovations.user_value: Book straight from search results.
innovations.relevance_reason: New patients search for dentists on maps and search engines.

innovations.title: No-show risk prediction
innovations.description: Score each booking's no-show risk so staff can remind or overbook carefully.
innovations.problem_solved: No-shows are not anticipated.
innovations.user_value: Fewer reminder messages for reliable patients.
risks: Bias against patient groups; needs history
innovations.relevance_reason: Visit history in ClinicDesk could predict no-shows; health-data rules (Q-005) apply.

innovations.title: Chat or voice booking assistant
innovations.description: Book, move or cancel appointments by chat or phone voice agent.
innovations.problem_solved: Phone bookings only during opening hours.
innovations.business_value: Takes load off the front desk.
innovations.user_value: Book by chat or phone at any hour.
innovations.relevance_reason: The swamped phone line is the client's stated problem; a voice or chat agent could take bookings.

innovations.title: Insurance eligibility check
innovations.description: Check a patient's insurance cover before the visit.
innovations.problem_solved: Cover surprises at the desk.
innovations.user_value: Know what is covered before the visit.
risks: Coverage varies by insurer and country
innovations.relevance_reason: Depends on the country and insurers (Q-005); valuable where dental insurance is common.

innovations.title: Field-level encryption
innovations.description: Encrypt the most sensitive fields so even database admins cannot read them.
innovations.problem_solved: Sensitive fields readable by anyone with database access.
innovations.user_value: Stronger protection of their data.
innovations.relevance_reason: Treatment type and identity together are sensitive health data.

innovations.title: Preventive care or maintenance nudges
innovations.description: Prompt people about preventive actions based on their history.
innovations.problem_solved: Preventive care is forgotten between visits.
innovations.user_value: Helpful prompts between check-ups.
innovations.relevance_reason: Oral-health reminders tied to visit history; must avoid giving medical advice.

innovations.title: Treatment-plan booking
innovations.description: Book every visit of a multi-step treatment plan in one go, sequenced as the dentist planned.
innovations.problem_solved: Multi-visit treatments are booked one call at a time.
innovations.business_value: Plans completed on time; fewer abandoned treatments.
innovations.user_value: All visits booked at once.
risks: BR-001 60-day window may cut a plan short
innovations.relevance_reason: Extends FR-001 beyond single check-ups; depends on what ClinicDesk exposes.

innovations.title: Family check-up day
innovations.description: Book back-to-back check-ups for a whole household in one trip.
innovations.problem_solved: Parents make separate calls and trips for each child.
innovations.user_value: One trip for the whole family.
innovations.relevance_reason: Families often share a dentist; needs a way to book for dependants (Q-004).

innovations.title: Smile timeline
innovations.description: Patients see their visit history and the dentist's shared notes and images over time.
innovations.problem_solved: Patients have no view of their own dental history.
innovations.business_value: Differentiates the practice; more engaged patients.
innovations.user_value: A personal record of their dental health.
innovations.relevance_reason: Builds on ClinicDesk records; only possible with patient identification and a known health-data regime.

trends.title: Online self-scheduling
trends.description: Customers expect to book, move and cancel appointments online at any hour.
trends.relevance_reason: The whole product is online self-scheduling; patients compare it with booking elsewhere.

trends.title: Two-way SMS appointment reminders
trends.description: Reminders customers can confirm or cancel by reply; widely used to cut no-shows.
trends.relevance_reason: Common answer to no-shows in dental practices; informs the reminders decision (Q-006).

trends.title: Core Web Vitals as the performance yardstick
trends.description: LCP, INP and CLS measured on real users are the common way to set web performance targets.
trends.relevance_reason: Gives the client a standard way to state the NFR-001 target.

trends.title: Accessibility laws for digital services
trends.description: Laws increasingly require WCAG-level accessibility for consumer-facing digital services.
trends.relevance_reason: A public healthcare booking page is likely covered; check which law applies (Q-005, Q-009).

trends.title: Passkeys replacing passwords
trends.description: Sign-in with device-bound WebAuthn credentials, supported by the major platforms.
trends.relevance_reason: An option for Q-004 if patient accounts are chosen; overkill for twice-yearly visits without accounts.

trends.title: SMS one-time codes as the only second factor
trends.description: SMS codes are vulnerable to SIM swap and phishing; services are moving to app, passkey or push factors.
trends.relevance_reason: If identity is checked by code, avoid SMS as the only factor for access to health data.

trends.title: Invisible bot protection instead of visual CAPTCHAs
trends.description: Risk-based, mostly invisible checks replace puzzles that block real users and fail accessibility.
trends.relevance_reason: Protects a login-free public page without hurting accessibility.

trends.title: Voice AI agents for phone calls
trends.description: AI agents answer phone calls and complete simple tasks such as booking.
trends.relevance_reason: Targets the client's real problem (busy phone line); maturity and patient acceptance need checking.

trends.title: Business messaging on WhatsApp and similar apps
trends.description: Customers are reached on chat apps they already use, with templates and opt-in.
trends.relevance_reason: Depends on the country (Q-005) and what patients there use.
